name: Paul Franklin
sources: Splice — Keeping the pedal steel guitar alive (https://splice.com/blog/keeping-pedal-steel-guitar-alive/)
Sound on Sound — Inside Track: Morgan Wallen & Post Malone (https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/inside-track-morgan-wallen-post-malone)
notes: The definitive modern pedal-steel voice, placed in PRODUCERS by the research as an *instrumental-grammar* entry: "Rich Redmond, Eddie Bayers, Shannon Forrest, Aaron Sterling, Brent Mason and Paul Franklin are placed in PRODUCERS as instrumental-grammar entries … no artist entry duplicates them" (Assignment notes). ⛔ **A second instruction depends on this file existing.** The Post Malone note says: "If a pop researcher has claimed Post Malone as an artist, drop my entry and keep the detail inside my **Aaron Sterling and Paul Franklin** entries, which carry the same session documentation." Post Malone was claimed by `pop-2020s`, so that fallback fired — and only one of its two named carriers was written. This is the other one. The defining capability is quoted and it is what the melodic blocks encode: "contrapuntal things like **simultaneously shifting voices within a chord up and down in pitch** without moving the bar" — oblique motion inside a sustained chord — so the line is step-dominated with almost no leaps, `chordToneBias` is the highest in this section, and the harmonic rhythm is slow because the chord is *held* while the voices move. The same sentence is why the chord block raises seventh and ninth shares: a voice moving inside a held triad is how those colours appear here, rather than as a different numeral. `articulation` and the humanize come from the volume-pedal fact — "maximum volume reached only **partway up the pedal's travel, with the remaining travel used for sustain**, which produces the instrument's signature swell-and-hold envelope" — plus the phrasing note that "a swell … peaks *after* the downbeat": a late, soft attack, which is a loose quantize and a wide velocity spread rather than a grid part. The counter sits an octave *below* the lead because the entry documents that register outright: "he expanded the instrument's register downward with a **baritone steel guitar tuned an octave below standard pedal steel**, plus … the 'Pedabro' … and 'The Box' … So the steel palette in this genre has three distinct registers/timbres, not one." Phrase placement is quoted twice — "entries in the gaps at phrase ends" and "answers vocal phrases in 2-bar gaps" — which is `phraseBars` and `fillGapsOnly`. The arrangement is the entry's own list: "steel takes the cold-open intro, answers vocal phrases in 2-bar gaps, holds pads under verses, and takes an **8-bar instrumental**" — ⚠ the engine's section vocabulary has no instrumental kind, so that 8-bar feature is carried by the bridge's length, and the cold open is the 2-bar intro. ⚠ **No `session.keys` is authored and the entry is the reason**: "he plays any key without repositioning logic changing, because the instrument's pedals and levers transpose voicings mechanically." ⚠ **No `session.bpm`**: the entry states no tempo band, so the genre's stands rather than an invented one. ⚠ **No `progressionFamilies`**: the entry names no numerals; only the voicing, the extension spread and the harmonic rhythm are authored from the contrapuntal description. ⚠ **No `bassline` block**: the entry's 808/bass line is about his *baritone steel*, not about a bass part, and that fact is spent on the counter's register instead — so the genre's bass is inherited rather than invented. ⚠ INFERRED: the melody register (a standard E9-neck span, not a measurement), the density range, the contour split, the counter ratio and every number in the chords block. ⚠ Confidence is medium (research: high) — instruments, technique and envelope behaviour are documented, but no tempo, key or numeral is, so the generator-facing numbers are this author's reading.
